claim: The piriform cortex (PCx) is essential for learning of odor information.
source: The piriform cortex (PCx) is essential for learning of odor information.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: The current view postulates that odor learning in the PCx is mainly due to plasticity in intracortical (IC) synapses.
source: The current view postulates that odor learning in the PCx is mainly due to plasticity in intracortical (IC) synapses, while odor information from the olfactory bulb carried via the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) is 'hardwired.'
evidence: This statement describes the prevailing view in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Odor information from the olfactory bulb carried via the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) is 'hardwired' according to the current view.
source: The current view postulates that odor learning in the PCx is mainly due to plasticity in intracortical (IC) synapses, while odor information from the olfactory bulb carried via the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) is 'hardwired.'
evidence: This statement describes the prevailing view that the authors challenge, supported by citations.

claim: Synaptic and optogenetically activated LOT synapses undergo strong and robust long-term potentiation (LTP) mediated by only a few local NMDA-spikes delivered at theta frequency.
source: We find that in contrast to the prevailing view, synaptic and optogenetically activated LOT synapses undergo strong and robust long-term potentiation (LTP) mediated by only a few local NMDA-spikes delivered at theta frequency, while global spike timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) protocols failed to induce LTP in these distal synapses.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3, 4, and 5.

claim: Global spike timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) protocols failed to induce LTP in distal LOT synapses.
source: We find that in contrast to the prevailing view, synaptic and optogenetically activated LOT synapses undergo strong and robust long-term potentiation (LTP) mediated by only a few local NMDA-spikes delivered at theta frequency, while global spike timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) protocols failed to induce LTP in these distal synapses.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: IC synapses in apical and basal dendrites undergo plasticity with both NMDA-spikes and STDP protocols.
source: In contrast, IC synapses in apical and basal dendrites undergo plasticity with both NMDA-spikes and STDP protocols but to a smaller extent compared with LOT synapses.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1, 2, 6, and 7.

claim: IC synapses undergo plasticity to a smaller extent compared with LOT synapses.
source: In contrast, IC synapses in apical and basal dendrites undergo plasticity with both NMDA-spikes and STDP protocols but to a smaller extent compared with LOT synapses.
evidence: This is a comparative finding supported by experimental data comparing different synapse types.

claim: The piriform cortex (PCx) is a main cortical station in olfactory processing.
source: The piriform cortex (PCx) is a main cortical station in olfactory processing, receiving direct odor information from the olfactory bulb (OB) via the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) as well as higher brain regions and is thought to be important for odor discrimination and recognition.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: PCx receives direct odor information from the olfactory bulb (OB) via the lateral olfactory tract (LOT).
source: The piriform cortex (PCx) is a main cortical station in olfactory processing, receiving direct odor information from the olfactory bulb (OB) via the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) as well as higher brain regions and is thought to be important for odor discrimination and recognition.
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge.

claim: PCx is thought to be important for odor discrimination and recognition.
source: The piriform cortex (PCx) is a main cortical station in olfactory processing, receiving direct odor information from the olfactory bulb (OB) via the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) as well as higher brain regions and is thought to be important for odor discrimination and recognition.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: Pyramidal neurons in the PCx serve as the main integration units within which the discrete molecular information channels are hypothesized to be recombined to form an 'odor object'.
source: Pyramidal neurons in the PCx serve as the main integration units within which the discrete molecular information channels are hypothesized to be recombined to form an 'odor object' (Wilson and Sullivan, 2011).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to Wilson and Sullivan, 2011.

claim: PCx pyramidal neurons receive direct afferent excitatory inputs from OB via the LOT, which terminate mainly on distal apical dendrites (layer Ia).
source: PCx pyramidal neurons receive two spatially distinct inputs that terminate on different compartments of their apical dendrites: first, the direct afferent excitatory inputs from OB via the LOT, which terminate mainly on distal apical dendrites (layer Ia).
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: PCx pyramidal neurons receive intracortical excitatory (IC) inputs from local PCx neurons and other cortical areas, which target the more proximal portions of the apical dendritic tree (layers Ib and II) and basal dendrites.
source: Second, intracortical excitatory (IC) inputs from local PCx neurons and other cortical areas, which target the more proximal portions of the apical dendritic tree (layers Ib and II) and basal dendrites (Bekkers and Suzuki, 2013; Haberly, 1985; Haberly, 2001; Haberly and Price, 1977; Isaacson, 2010; Neville and Haberly, 2004; Suzuki and Bekkers, 2006).
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Synaptic plasticity rules have crucial role in determining the way cortical networks acquire, organize, and store information.
source: Synaptic plasticity rules have crucial role in determining the way cortical networks acquire, organize, and store information.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: PCx mediates learning and recall of olfactory information.
source: It is postulated that PCx mediates learning and recall of olfactory information (Franks and Isaacson, 2005; Haberly, 1985; Haberly, 2001; Saar et al., 1998; Saar et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: IC synapses of PCx pyramidal neurons undergo plasticity changes similar to neocortical and hippocampal pyramidal neurons.
source: Previous studies have shown that similar to neocortical and hippocampal pyramidal neurons (Bliss and Collingridge, 1993; Feldman, 2012; Sjöström et al., 2007), IC synapses of PCx pyramidal neurons undergo plasticity changes.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: NMDA-R-dependent long-term potentiation (LTP) was robustly observed in IC synapses both when stimulated by theta rhythm alone or when paired with either a burst of LOT activation or back-propagating action potentials (BAPs) using spike timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) protocols.
source: NMDA-R-dependent long-term potentiation (LTP) was robustly observed in IC synapses both when stimulated by theta rhythm alone (Haberly et al., 1994) or when paired with either a burst of LOT activation (Kanter and Haberly, 1990; Kanter and Haberly, 1993; Kanter et al., 1996), or back-propagating action potentials (BAPs) using spike timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) protocols (Johenning et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Following olfactory rule learning in vivo, PCx pyramidal neurons exhibited increase in IC synaptic strength and excitability.
source: In line with the importance of IC plasticity changes in learning, it was shown that following olfactory rule learning in vivo, PCx pyramidal neurons exhibited increase in IC synaptic strength and excitability (Lebel et al., 2001; Saar and Barkai, 2003; Saar and Barkai, 2009; Saar et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations to in vivo studies.

claim: Plasticity of afferent LOT synapses is yet an unresolved issue.
source: In contrast to IC inputs, plasticity of afferent LOT synapses is yet an unresolved issue (Haberly et al., 1994; Jung et al., 1990; Roman et al., 1993).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations indicating conflicting or incomplete findings in the literature.

claim: NMDA-dependent LTP using theta burst stimulation of LOT inputs was less robust and weak, with typically 10–15% potentiation observed in afferent fibers after a single theta burst train, with saturation of 12–25% after multiple trains.
source: NMDA-dependent LTP using theta burst stimulation of LOT inputs was less robust and weak. Typically, 10–15% potentiation was observed in afferent fibers after a single theta burst train, with saturation of 12–25% after multiple trains (Franks and Isaacson, 2005; Jung et al., 1990; Kanter and Haberly, 1990; Poo and Isaacson, 2007; Roman et al., 1993).
evidence: This is a statement summarizing findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: STDP protocols failed altogether to induce LTP in LOT synapses because of the severe attenuation of BAPs to distal apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons, where LOT inputs terminate.
source: STDP protocols failed altogether to induce LTP in LOT synapses because of the severe attenuation of BAPs to distal apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons, where LOT inputs terminate (Haberly, 2001; Neville and Haberly, 2004).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations explaining the mechanism for STDP failure.

claim: LOT synapses located in distal apical dendrites are considered for the most part to be 'hardwired' after the sensory critical period.
source: Currently, LOT synapses located in distal apical dendrites are considered for the most part to be 'hardwired' after the sensory critical period (Bekkers and Suzuki, 2013; Franks and Isaacson, 2005), and robust NMDA-R-dependent LTP is limited to a brief postnatal time window of approximately 4 weeks (Franks and Isaacson, 2005; Poo and Isaacson, 2007), which is in contrast to IC synapses that retain the capacity for plasticity throughout adulthood.
evidence: This is a statement of the prevailing view supported by citations.

claim: Robust NMDA-R-dependent LTP in LOT synapses is limited to a brief postnatal time window of approximately 4 weeks.
source: Currently, LOT synapses located in distal apical dendrites are considered for the most part to be 'hardwired' after the sensory critical period (Bekkers and Suzuki, 2013; Franks and Isaacson, 2005), and robust NMDA-R-dependent LTP is limited to a brief postnatal time window of approximately 4 weeks (Franks and Isaacson, 2005; Poo and Isaacson, 2007), which is in contrast to IC synapses that retain the capacity for plasticity throughout adulthood.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: IC synapses retain the capacity for plasticity throughout adulthood.
source: Currently, LOT synapses located in distal apical dendrites are considered for the most part to be 'hardwired' after the sensory critical period (Bekkers and Suzuki, 2013; Franks and Isaacson, 2005), and robust NMDA-R-dependent LTP is limited to a brief postnatal time window of approximately 4 weeks (Franks and Isaacson, 2005; Poo and Isaacson, 2007), which is in contrast to IC synapses that retain the capacity for plasticity throughout adulthood.
evidence: This is a statement supported by inference from cited studies.

claim: The notion of LOT synapse stability in adulthood is in conflict with reports obtained in vivo during complex olfactory learning.
source: Yet, the notion of LOT synapse stability in adulthood is in conflict with reports obtained in vivo during complex olfactory learning (Cohen et al., 2008; Cohen et al., 2015; Patneau and Stripling, 1992).
evidence: This is a statement identifying a conflict in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: Local NMDA-spikes are generated in distal apical dendrites by activation of LOT synapses.
source: We have recently reported the generation of local NMDA-spikes in distal apical dendrites by activation of LOT synapses (Kumar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement referring to a previous finding by the authors.

claim: Dendritic NMDA-spikes generate large localized calcium transients, which can serve as postsynaptic signals for LTP induction in the activated LOT synapses.
source: These dendritic NMDA-spikes generate large localized calcium transients, which can serve as postsynaptic signals for LTP induction in the activated LOT synapses.
evidence: This is a statement based on inference from the properties of NMDA-spikes.

claim: NMDA-spikes were critical for inducing LTP in the dendrites of CA3 pyramidal neurons.
source: In support of this hypothesis, it was recently shown that NMDA-spikes were critical for inducing LTP in the dendrites of CA3 pyramidal neurons (Brandalise et al., 2016) and in layer 2–3 pyramidal neurons of somatosensory cortex in vivo (Gambino et al., 2014; Gordon et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: NMDA-spikes were critical for inducing LTP in layer 2–3 pyramidal neurons of somatosensory cortex in vivo.
source: In support of this hypothesis, it was recently shown that NMDA-spikes were critical for inducing LTP in the dendrites of CA3 pyramidal neurons (Brandalise et al., 2016) and in layer 2–3 pyramidal neurons of somatosensory cortex in vivo (Gambino et al., 2014; Gordon et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Synchronized firing of spatially clustered afferent LOT synapses can generate local NMDA-spikes, which in turn can trigger LTP of the activated synapses in distal dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons.
source: We thus hypothesized that synchronized firing of spatially clustered afferent LOT synapses can generate local NMDA-spikes, which in turn can trigger LTP of the activated synapses in distal dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is the main hypothesis of the study.

claim: Local NMDA-spikes generated in distal apical dendrites delivered at 4 Hz can induce robust and strong LTP (>200%) of LOT inputs impinging on distal apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis and settling the inconsistencies in the literature, we found that local NMDA-spikes generated in distal apical dendrites delivered at 4 Hz mimicking the exploratory sniff cycle in rats (Wilson, 1998) can induce robust and strong LTP (>200%) of LOT inputs impinging on distal apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: 4 Hz mimics the exploratory sniff cycle in rats.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis and settling the inconsistencies in the literature, we found that local NMDA-spikes generated in distal apical dendrites delivered at 4 Hz mimicking the exploratory sniff cycle in rats (Wilson, 1998) can induce robust and strong LTP (>200%) of LOT inputs impinging on distal apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to Wilson, 1998.

claim: Only a few NMDA-spikes (as low as two NMDA-spikes) were required for potentiation of LOT inputs.
source: Only a few NMDA-spikes (as low as two NMDA-spikes) were required for potentiation of LOT inputs.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: STDP protocol failed to induce LTP of LOT synapses.
source: As previously described, STDP protocol failed to induce LTP of LOT synapses (Johenning et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation and confirmed by the authors' data.

claim: For IC apical and basal synapses, potentiation was mediated by both NMDA-spikes and STDP protocols, but the magnitude of potentiation was smaller compared to that of LOT synapses.
source: In contrast, for IC apical and basal synapses, potentiation was mediated by both NMDA-spikes and STDP protocols, but the magnitude of potentiation was smaller compared to that of LOT synapses.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1, 2, 6, and 7.

claim: The inputs to PCx are highly segregated along the axis of apical dendrites in principal pyramidal neurons.
source: The inputs to PCx are highly segregated along the axis of apical dendrites in principal pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Location specific plasticity rules have been previously shown for neocortical pyramidal dendrites.
source: This raises the possibility of location specific plasticity rules as was previously shown for neocortical pyramidal dendrites (Gordon et al., 2006; Kampa et al., 2007; Letzkus et al., 2006; Letzkus et al., 2007; Lisman and Spruston, 2010; Sandler et al., 2016; Sjöström and Häusser, 2006; Sjöström et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: STDP paradigm failed to induce LTP in distally activated apical synapses at layer Ia where most of the LOT inputs terminate.
source: In accordance with a previous report (Johenning et al., 2009), this paradigm failed to induce LTP in distally activated apical synapses at layer Ia where most of the LOT inputs terminate (Figure 1C and D; the EPSP amplitude after the induction protocol was 103.06% ± 2.81% of the control EPSP; p=0.7658; n = 11).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: The EPSP amplitude after the STDP induction protocol in distal layer Ia inputs was 103.06% ± 2.81% of the control EPSP (p=0.7658; n = 11).
source: In accordance with a previous report (Johenning et al., 2009), this paradigm failed to induce LTP in distally activated apical synapses at layer Ia where most of the LOT inputs terminate (Figure 1C and D; the EPSP amplitude after the induction protocol was 103.06% ± 2.81% of the control EPSP; p=0.7658; n = 11).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 1.

claim: When paired with an EPSP, STDP protocol using synaptically evoked postsynaptic APs also failed to potentiate distally located layer Ia inputs (104.99% ± 3.86% of control; p=0.7577, n = 3).
source: Next, we replaced APs evoked by somatic current injection with postsynaptic APs evoked by synaptic stimulation in layer IIa (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). When paired with an EPSP (as described in Figure 1B), this STDP protocol also failed to potentiate distally located layer Ia inputs (104.99% ± 3.86% of control; p=0.7577, n = 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Using the same STDP protocol but activating IC instead of LOT synapses at more proximal apical dendritic locations induced robust potentiation of layer Ib inputs (168.93% ± 6.54% of control EPSP; p=0.01387, n = 6).
source: In sharp contrast, using the same protocol but activating IC instead of LOT synapses at more proximal apical dendritic locations induced robust potentiation of layer Ib inputs (Figure 1F and G; 168.93% ± 6.54% of control EPSP; p=0.01387, n = 6).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: PCx pyramidal neurons possess an elaborated basal dendritic arbor.
source: PCx pyramidal neurons also possess an elaborated basal dendritic arbor (Suzuki and Bekkers, 2006).
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Basal dendrites receive IC inputs, mainly feedback inputs from local neurons in PCx and other olfactory areas.
source: These dendrites receive IC inputs, mainly feedback inputs from local neurons in PCx and other olfactory areas (Hagiwara et al., 2012; Isaacson, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: STDP protocol induced significant LTP in basally located synapses (137.12% ± 6.11% of control EPSP; p=0.0031, n = 8), with a relatively smaller magnitude compared to potentiation values in proximal apical dendrites (p=0.00427).
source: We observed a significant LTP in these basally located synapses, however, with a relatively smaller magnitude (Figure 2B–D; 137.12% ± 6.11% of control EPSP; p=0.0031, n = 8) compared to potentiation values in proximal apical dendrites (p=0.00427) using the same induction protocol.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 2.

claim: The STDP burst protocol is efficient in inducing robust LTP in IC inputs both at proximal apical locations and basal synapses but fails altogether to induce LTP at LOT synapses located on distal apical dendrites.
source: Thus, the STDP burst protocol is efficient in inducing robust LTP in IC inputs both at proximal apical locations and basal synapses but fails altogether to induce LTP at LOT synapses located on distal apical dendrites.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data from Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Dendritic spikes are excellent candidates for serving as a local postsynaptic signal for induction of long-term synaptic plasticity.
source: Dendritic spikes are excellent candidates for serving as a local postsynaptic signal for induction of long-term synaptic plasticity (Gambino et al., 2014; Golding et al., 2002; Gordon et al., 2006; Lisman and Spruston, 2005; Lisman and Spruston, 2010; Major et al., 2013; Polsky et al., 2009; Remy and Spruston, 2007).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: Local NMDA-spike induction protocol (2–7 local NMDA-spikes repeated at 4 Hz) was very efficient in inducing robust and strong LTP of EPSPs in the distal LOT synapses terminating in layer Ia (213.98% ± 10.81%; p=0.0000687; n = 26).
source: This local induction protocol was very efficient in inducing robust and strong LTP of EPSPs in the distal LOT synapses terminating in layer Ia (213.98% ± 10.81%; p=0.0000687; n = 26; Figure 3D and F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 3.

claim: As few as two full-blown NMDA-spikes at 4 Hz were enough to cause potentiation, which lasted for the length of the recording (>75 min).
source: As few as two full-blown NMDA-spikes at 4 Hz were enough to cause potentiation (Figure 3E), which lasted for the length of the recording (>75 min).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: EPSP subthreshold to NMDA-spike initiation delivered with same induction protocol failed to evoke potentiation of the LOT inputs (106.79% ± 5.69% of the control EPSP; p=0.8373, n = 5 cells).
source: EPSP subthreshold to NMDA-spike initiation delivered with same induction protocol failed to evoke potentiation of the LOT inputs (Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B). The average EPSP amplitude after sub-NMDA-spike induction was 106.79% ± 5.69% of the control EPSP (p=0.8373, n = 5 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In experiments where NMDA-spikes were blocked by application of the NMDA-R antagonist DL-2-amino-5-phosphonovaleric acid (APV; 50 µM), LOT synapses failed to undergo potentiation using the same induction protocol (95.06% ± 4.69% of control EPSP; p=0.817, n = 5).
source: Also, in experiments where NMDA-spikes were blocked by application of the NMDA-R antagonist DL-2-amino-5-phosphonovaleric acid (APV; 50 µM), LOT synapses failed to undergo potentiation using the same induction protocol (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D). The EPSP amplitude post induction was 95.06% ± 4.69% of control EPSP in the presence of APV (p=0.817, n = 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Application of baclofen (100 µM) did not change the resting membrane potential and did not alter the chances of occurrence of NMDA-spikes.
source: Application of baclofen did not change the resting membrane potential and did not alter the chances of occurrence of NMDA-spikes (Kumar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Bursts of NMDA-spikes delivered at 4 Hz in the presence of baclofen caused potentiation of layer Ia inputs (236.57% ± 17.51% of the control EPSP recorded at 0.033 Hz; p=0.0246; n = 5 cells).
source: Bursts of NMDA-spikes delivered at 4 Hz in the presence of baclofen also caused potentiation of layer Ia inputs (Figure 4A–D; 236.57% ± 17.51% of the control EPSP recorded at 0.033 Hz; p=0.0246; n = 5 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 4.

claim: Only three pairings of opto-EPSPs and NMDA-spikes were sufficient in inducing robust and strong LTP of the LOT inputs (232.45% ± 16.55%; p=0.000286; n = 11).
source: Only three pairings of opto-EPSPs and NMDA-spikes were sufficient in inducing robust and strong LTP of the LOT inputs (232.45% ± 16.55%; p=0.000286; n = 11; Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 5.

claim: NMDA-spike induction protocol (4–10 NMDA-spikes at 4 Hz) induced potentiation of proximal apical IC synapses (127 ± 4.39 µm from soma), but to a smaller extent compared to distal apical LOT synapses and even smaller than potentiation induced by STDP protocol in these IC synapses.
source: A similar NMDA-spike induction protocol (4–10 NMDA-spikes at 4 Hz) also induced potentiation of proximal apical IC synapses (127 ± 4.39 µm from soma) (Figure 6A–D), but to a smaller extent compared to distal apical LOT synapses and even smaller than potentiation induced by STDP protocol in these IC synapses.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Post induction, the apical IC EPSP amplitude was 148.48% ± 4.1% of the control (p=0.00204; n = 9; p=0.0013 for comparison of proximal versus distal NMDA-spike potentiation; p=0.0127 for comparison with STDP in IC synapses).
source: Post induction, the apical IC EPSP amplitude was 148.48% ± 4.1% of the control (Figure 6F; p=0.00204; n = 9; p=0.0013 for comparison of proximal versus distal NMDA-spike potentiation; p=0.0127 for comparison with STDP in IC synapses).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 6.

claim: Full-blown NMDA-spikes initiated at proximal apical locations were accompanied with BAPs.
source: Typically, full-blown NMDA-spikes initiated at these proximal apical locations were accompanied with BAPs (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiment shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Pairing of BAPs and local EPSPs for five repetitions (one EPSP paired with three BAPs at 150 Hz repeated five times at 4 Hz) did not induce potentiation of proximal IC synapses.
source: To control for the contribution of these BAPs, we repeated the induction protocol, but instead of using NMDA-spikes we used pairing of BAPs and local EPSPs for five repetitions (one EPSP paired with three BAPs at 150 Hz repeated five times at 4 Hz). In this case, we did not observe potentiation of these proximal IC synapses (Figure 6G), thus we concluded that NMDA-spikes were crucial for the potentiation of IC synapses with the NMDA-spike protocol.
evidence: This is a finding from the control experiment shown in Figure 6G.

claim: NMDA-spikes were crucial for the potentiation of IC synapses with the NMDA-spike protocol.
source: To control for the contribution of these BAPs, we repeated the induction protocol, but instead of using NMDA-spikes we used pairing of BAPs and local EPSPs for five repetitions (one EPSP paired with three BAPs at 150 Hz repeated five times at 4 Hz). In this case, we did not observe potentiation of these proximal IC synapses (Figure 6G), thus we concluded that NMDA-spikes were crucial for the potentiation of IC synapses with the NMDA-spike protocol.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the control experiment shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Calcium transients evoked by NMDA-spikes both in spines and adjacent shafts were significantly larger than those evoked by STDP stimulation (p<0.0001).
source: Interestingly, calcium transients evoked by NMDA-spikes both in spines and adjacent shafts were significantly larger than those evoked by STDP stimulation (Figure 6E and H; p<0.0001), yet the degree of potentiation with STDP protocol was higher (p=0.0127) compared to the NMDA-spike protocol.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 6E and H.

claim: The degree of potentiation with STDP protocol was higher (p=0.0127) compared to the NMDA-spike protocol in proximal IC synapses.
source: Interestingly, calcium transients evoked by NMDA-spikes both in spines and adjacent shafts were significantly larger than those evoked by STDP stimulation (Figure 6E and H; p<0.0001), yet the degree of potentiation with STDP protocol was higher (p=0.0127) compared to the NMDA-spike protocol.
evidence: This is a quantitative result comparing two experimental conditions.

claim: The amount of calcium entry per se is not the only variable determining the degree of potentiation.
source: This result indicates that the amount of calcium entry per se is not the only variable determining the degree of potentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that larger calcium transients did not result in greater potentiation.

claim: Basal dendrites in PCx pyramidal neurons are a major target for IC connections.
source: Basal dendrites in PCx pyramidal neurons are also a major target for IC connections (Haberly, 1985; Isaacson, 2010; Luskin and Price, 1983a; Luskin and Price, 1983b).
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Dendritic NMDA-spikes were evoked in basal dendrites of PCx neurons.
source: Similar to apical dendrites, dendritic NMDA-spikes were evoked in basal dendrites of PCx neurons (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The average spike threshold recorded at the soma for basal dendrite NMDA-spikes was 10.2 ± 1.6 mV.
source: The average spike threshold recorded at the soma was 10.2 ± 1.6 mV.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experiment.

claim: The dendritic spike amplitude and area as measured at the soma for basal dendrite NMDA-spikes was 27.2 ± 2.5 mV and 2999.5 ± 434.7 mV * ms, respectively (n = 6 cells).
source: The dendritic spike amplitude and area as measured at the soma was 27.2 ± 2.5 mV and 2999.5 ± 434.7 mV * ms, respectively (n = 6 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experiment.

claim: NMDA-spike induction protocol significantly potentiated the IC synapses on basal dendrites (140.64% ± 4.5% of the control; p=0.006526, n = 6 cells).
source: Using the same NMDA-spike induction protocol used for apical dendrites significantly potentiated the IC synapses on basal dendrites (Figure 7C; 140.64% ± 4.5% of the control; p=0.006526, n = 6 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The degree of potentiation in basal dendrites was smaller compared to that of LOT inputs in distal apical dendrites.
source: However, the degree of potentiation was smaller compared to that of LOT inputs in distal apical dendrites (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a comparative finding from the experiments.

claim: EPSPs that were subthreshold for NMDA-spikes failed to induce significant potentiation of the EPSPs in basal dendrites (108.73% ± 3.13% of the control EPSP, p=0.8253, n = 5).
source: EPSPs that were subthreshold for NMDA-spikes failed to induce significant potentiation of the EPSPs (108.73% ± 3.13% of the control EPSP, p=0.8253, n = 5; Figure 7F and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 7F and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The same induction protocol in the presence of NMDA-R blocker APV (50 µM) failed to cause potentiation at basal synapses (100.69% ± 4.27% of control, p=0.9948, n = 5).
source: The same induction protocol in the presence of NMDA-R blocker APV (50 µM) failed to cause potentiation at these basal synapses (100.69% ± 4.27% of control, p=0.9948, n = 5; Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Local NMDA-spikes are necessary for inducing potentiation of basal inputs.
source: These results indicate that local NMDA-spikes are necessary for inducing potentiation of basal inputs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results showing that blocking NMDA-spikes prevents potentiation.

claim: LOT inputs become 'hardwired' after the olfactory critical period according to the notion challenged by the authors.
source: Here, we challenge the notion that LOT inputs become 'hardwired' after the olfactory critical period (Franks and Isaacson, 2005; Kanter and Haberly, 1993; Poo and Isaacson, 2007), and only IC inputs undergo plasticity changes in adulthood.
evidence: This is a statement of the prevailing view that the authors challenge, supported by citations.

claim: Only IC inputs undergo plasticity changes in adulthood according to the notion challenged by the authors.
source: Here, we challenge the notion that LOT inputs become 'hardwired' after the olfactory critical period (Franks and Isaacson, 2005; Kanter and Haberly, 1993; Poo and Isaacson, 2007), and only IC inputs undergo plasticity changes in adulthood.
evidence: This is a statement of the prevailing view that the authors challenge.

claim: LOT inputs contacting distal apical PCx pyramidal neuron dendrites do not undergo significant LTP when paired with somatic output activation using STDP plasticity protocols.
source: We show that while LOT inputs contacting distal apical PCx pyramidal neuron dendrites do not undergo significant LTP when paired with somatic output activation using STDP plasticity protocols, they undergo strong and robust LTP when co-activated with other spatially clustered LOT inputs that generate local NMDA-spikes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: LOT inputs undergo strong and robust LTP when co-activated with other spatially clustered LOT inputs that generate local NMDA-spikes.
source: We show that while LOT inputs contacting distal apical PCx pyramidal neuron dendrites do not undergo significant LTP when paired with somatic output activation using STDP plasticity protocols, they undergo strong and robust LTP when co-activated with other spatially clustered LOT inputs that generate local NMDA-spikes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Only a few (≥2) NMDA-spikes are necessary for full-blown LTP induction in distal LOT synapses.
source: Only a few (≥2) NMDA-spikes are necessary for full-blown LTP induction in these distal LOT synapses.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The failure to induce LTP with STDP protocols in distally located LOT synapses is in line with reports from other types of pyramidal neurons.
source: The failure to induce LTP with STDP protocols in distally located LOT synapses is in line with reports from other types of pyramidal neurons (Gordon et al., 2006; Kampa et al., 2007; Larkum et al., 2009; Letzkus et al., 2006; Nevian et al., 2007; Sandler et al., 2016; Sjöström and Häusser, 2006; Sjöström et al., 2008) and is consistent with the severe attenuation of BAPs to the distal portions of the apical tree (Bathellier et al., 2009; Johenning et al., 2009; Kumar et al., 2018) and with the high density of A-type potassium channels in the distal apical tree of PCx neurons (Johenning et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The failure to induce LTP with STDP protocols in distally located LOT synapses is consistent with the severe attenuation of BAPs to the distal portions of the apical tree.
source: The failure to induce LTP with STDP protocols in distally located LOT synapses is in line with reports from other types of pyramidal neurons (Gordon et al., 2006; Kampa et al., 2007; Larkum et al., 2009; Letzkus et al., 2006; Nevian et al., 2007; Sandler et al., 2016; Sjöström and Häusser, 2006; Sjöström et al., 2008) and is consistent with the severe attenuation of BAPs to the distal portions of the apical tree (Bathellier et al., 2009; Johenning et al., 2009; Kumar et al., 2018) and with the high density of A-type potassium channels in the distal apical tree of PCx neurons (Johenning et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations explaining the mechanism.

claim: There is a high density of A-type potassium channels in the distal apical tree of PCx neurons.
source: The failure to induce LTP with STDP protocols in distally located LOT synapses is in line with reports from other types of pyramidal neurons (Gordon et al., 2006; Kampa et al., 2007; Larkum et al., 2009; Letzkus et al., 2006; Nevian et al., 2007; Sandler et al., 2016; Sjöström and Häusser, 2006; Sjöström et al., 2008) and is consistent with the severe attenuation of BAPs to the distal portions of the apical tree (Bathellier et al., 2009; Johenning et al., 2009; Kumar et al., 2018) and with the high density of A-type potassium channels in the distal apical tree of PCx neurons (Johenning et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation.

claim: NMDA-spikes powerfully depolarize the distal locations of the apical tree and are associated with large calcium influx locally.
source: NMDA-spikes powerfully depolarize the distal locations of the apical tree and are associated with large calcium influx locally (Kumar et al., 2018; Major et al., 2008), and thus serve as a strong postsynaptic signal for induction of plasticity.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: NMDA-spikes serve as a strong postsynaptic signal for induction of plasticity.
source: NMDA-spikes powerfully depolarize the distal locations of the apical tree and are associated with large calcium influx locally (Kumar et al., 2018; Major et al., 2008), and thus serve as a strong postsynaptic signal for induction of plasticity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the properties of NMDA-spikes and supported by citations.

claim: The results are consistent with a previous study in CA3 pyramidal neurons showing the necessity of local NMDA-spikes for plasticity in these neurons.
source: Our results are consistent with a previous study in CA3 pyramidal neurons showing the necessity of local NMDA-spikes for plasticity in these neurons (Brandalise et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement comparing the current findings to a previous study.

claim: Dendritic spikes in general can serve as strong and efficient mediators for LTP in CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Moreover, similar to our findings, previous reports show that dendritic spikes in general can serve as strong and efficient mediators for LTP in CA1 pyramidal neurons (Remy and Spruston, 2007).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The results are consistent with in vivo data showing enhanced strength between the OB inputs and the PCx during olfactory learning in adulthood.
source: Importantly, our results are also consistent with in vivo data showing enhanced strength between the OB inputs and the PCx during olfactory learning in adulthood (Chu et al., 2016; Cohen et al., 2008; Cohen et al., 2015; Roman et al., 1993).
evidence: This is a statement comparing the current findings to in vivo studies.

claim: The reason for the inability of prior studies to induce robust LTP of LOT inputs was related to the fact their induction protocols did not reliably generate local NMDA-spikes in distal apical dendrites.
source: We assume that the reason for the inability of prior studies to induce robust LTP of LOT inputs was related to the fact their induction protocols did not reliably generate local NMDA-spikes in distal apical dendrites (Franks and Isaacson, 2005; Kanter and Haberly, 1993; Poo and Isaacson, 2007).
evidence: This is an inference based on the current findings and comparison to previous studies.

claim: The results are consistent with a mechanism where NMDA-spike-mediated potentiation of co-activated LOT synapses clustered on the same dendritic segment can be used for storage of different olfactory combinations onto different dendritic branches.
source: Our results thus are consistent with a mechanism where NMDA-spike-mediated potentiation of co-activated LOT synapses clustered on the same dendritic segment can be used for storage of different olfactory combinations onto different dendritic branches (Kumar et al., 2018; Poirazi et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings and supported by citations.

claim: Despite the significantly larger calcium influx evoked by NMDA-spikes compared with STDP, the degree of potentiation of apical IC synapses was smaller with NMDA-spike protocol compared with STDP.
source: In proximal IC synapses, we find that despite the significantly larger calcium influx evoked by NMDA-spikes compared with STDP, the degree of potentiation of apical IC synapses was smaller with NMDA-spike protocol compared with STDP.
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments comparing NMDA-spike and STDP protocols.

claim: The kinetics and source of calcium entry may also influence potentiation.
source: The kinetics and source of calcium entry may also influence potentiation (Inglebert and Debanne, 2021; Zhou et al., 2005), as well as possible involvement of neuromodulators.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations suggesting additional factors that may influence potentiation.

claim: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) was a necessary requirement to gate plasticity in distal basal dendrites of layer 2–3 neocortical pyramidal neurons in addition to calcium entry.
source: See, for example, Gordon et al., 2006, where we showed that in distal basal dendrites of layer 2–3 neocortical pyramidal neurons, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) was a necessary requirement to gate plasticity in addition to calcium entry.

claim: The anatomical arrangement of the OB LOT inputs is such that these inputs terminate broadly throughout the PCx and single pyramidal neurons receive inputs from multiple broadly distributed olfactory glomeruli.
source: The anatomical arrangement of the OB LOT inputs is such that these inputs terminate broadly throughout the PCx and single pyramidal neurons receive inputs from multiple broadly distributed olfactory glomeruli (Miyamichi et al., 2011; Nagayama et al., 2010; Sosulski et al., 2011).

claim: This anatomical arrangement enables a large space of odor combinations to randomly terminate on different neurons and dendritic branches of PCx pyramidal neurons.
source: This anatomical arrangement enables a large space of odor combinations to randomly terminate on different neurons and dendritic branches of PCx pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical arrangement described.

claim: A leading theory of odor learning in PCx postulates that an odor representation is generated via strengthening of IC recurrent synapses activated during odor presentation, thus forming odor-specific ensembles in the PCx.
source: A leading theory of odor learning in PCx postulates that an odor representation is generated via strengthening of IC recurrent synapses activated during odor presentation, thus forming odor-specific ensembles in the PCx (Haberly, 2001; Hasselmo and Barkai, 1995; Wilson and Sullivan, 2011).

claim: The specificity to odor is enabled by strengthening the connectivity only between neurons that respond to the same set of LOT inputs.
source: The specificity to odor is enabled by strengthening the connectivity only between neurons that respond to the same set of LOT inputs.

source: Upon exposure to the odor, these neurons will fire, and as a result the connectivity between these neurons will be strengthened by associative LTP mechanisms.

claim: Upon repeated exposures to the odor, a stronger and more robust activation of this odor-specific neuronal ensemble will take place due to the potentiated IC recurrent connections.
source: Upon repeated exposures to the odor, a stronger and more robust activation of this odor-specific neuronal ensemble will take place due to the potentiated IC recurrent connections (Haberly, 2001).

claim: LOT inputs coding for a specific odor and terminating on the same distal dendritic branch could be self-potentiated via the NMDA-spike mechanism and a memory trace of the odor will be formed in PCx.

source: Such a mechanism is consistent with the in vivo findings showing potentiation of bulb inputs to PCx during complex olfactory learning (Cohen et al., 2008; Cohen et al., 2015).

source: NMDA-spike-based plasticity of LOT inputs can potentially contribute to odor representation in multiple ways: first, formation of an odor memory trace at the LOT with branch-specific dendritic plasticity mechanisms will increase the computational and storage capacity of PCx neurons (Weber et al., 2016; Wu and Mel, 2009).

claim: Instead of a cell assembly representing a single odor, it can be stored in single dendrites.
